GAQ327R291
Accounting Data & Technology Manager
About the Role
We are building a finance function that stays ahead of the curve — leveraging AI, automation, and modern tooling to operate at the pace Databricks demands. We are seeking an Accounting Data & Technology Manager to join our Global Accounting team and serve as the architect of the redesign of our accounting processes by building automation solutions and managing data pipelines that power our global accounting organization. You will serve as the accounting team's S/4HANA expert — the person who ensures our in-flight SAP implementation reflects best practice rather than a lift-and-shift of how we operate in NetSuite today.
You will be responsible for bridging the gap between our team's subject matter experts, our technology solutions, and the business data needed to support accounting operations. In addition to SAP ownership, this role will build purposeful, reliable solutions on top of the Databricks platform and Finance Datalake to accelerate global accounting operations.
During the SAP implementation, you will work alongside our system integrator to challenge design decisions, identify where SAP's native capabilities can replace manual workarounds, and ensure the accounting team is building on the right foundation from day one.
Post go-live, the role transitions to continuous improvement — owning automation opportunities, streamlining close processes as SAP capabilities evolve, and ensuring Databricks is getting progressively more value out of the platform over time rather than running it as a static system.
This is a rare opportunity to shape a major ERP platform from day one at one of the world's fastest-growing technology companies, with the autonomy to define how SAP works for accounting at Databricks — and how it connects to the most advanced data and AI platform in the market.
What You'll Do
SAP Implementation Governance (Near-Term)
Work alongside our system integrator as the accounting team's internal SAP S/4HANA subject matter expert throughout the implementation program.
Challenge design decisions and configuration choices — ensuring they reflect SAP best practice rather than replicating current-state NetSuite processes.
Identify where SAP's native capabilities (standard workflows, automated postings, embedded analytics, Fiori apps) can replace manual workarounds and custom development.
Own the accounting team's requirements, testing, and sign-off for SAP configuration across core FICO areas — general ledger, accounts payable, accounts receivable, fixed assets, and close management.
Partner with our system integrator, IT and Finance Transformation to ensure data migration, chart of accounts design, and master data governance meet accounting's needs.
Continuous Improvement & Optimization (Post Go-Live)
Own the SAP continuous improvement roadmap for accounting — identifying automation opportunities, process simplifications, and new SAP capabilities as they are released.
Streamline close processes within SAP — driving adoption of native automation, reducing cycle time, eliminating manual steps, and improving data quality with each close cycle.
Monitor system performance and proactively address configuration issues, data quality gaps, and process bottlenecks.
Collaborate with Tax, Treasury, FP&A, Accounts Payable, Revenue, and Procurement to ensure SAP configuration supports end-to-end finance processes — not just accounting in isolation.
Ensure SOX-relevant system controls (automated, access and change management controls) within SAP are properly configured, documented, and operating effectively.
SAP × Databricks Platform Integration
Own the design and governance of how SAP accounting data flows into the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform — ensuring clean, timely, and well-structured data for financial reporting, analytics, and AI use cases.
Partner with Data Engineering and Finance Systems to define the SAP-to-Databricks integration architecture — including extraction patterns, data models, and refresh cadences that support close timelines and ad-hoc analysis.
Identify opportunities to leverage Databricks' AI and automation capabilities on top of SAP data — such as anomaly detection on journal entries, predictive accruals, automated reconciliation matching, and natural-language reporting via Genie.
Serve as the accounting team's voice in shaping how Databricks' own platform is used for internal finance operations — ensuring the company is a best-practice reference customer for its own technology.
What We're Looking For
Required Qualifications
8+ years of progressive experience in accounting systems, ERP administration, or finance technology — with deep, hands-on SAP S/4HANA FICO experience.
Demonstrated expertise in SAP S/4HANA configuration across core accounting areas: general ledger, accounts payable, accounts receivable, fixed assets, and financial close and consolidation.
Experience participating in or leading at least one full-cycle SAP S/4HANA implementation — ideally on the business/functional side rather than purely technical.
Strong understanding of accounting close processes, U.S. GAAP, and how ERP configuration decisions impact financial reporting.
Experience with SAP master data governance, chart of accounts design, and configuration documentation.
SOX experience — understanding how system controls, access management, and segregation of duties operate within SAP.
Ability to translate between accounting business requirements and SAP technical configuration — comfortable working with both accountants and technical consultants.
Strong communication skills — able to articulate system design trade-offs to senior finance leadership clearly and concisely.
High ownership, attention to detail, and the ability to work independently without constant direction.
Preferred Qualifications
SAP S/4HANA certification (e.g., SAP Certified Application Associate — Financial Accounting).
Experience with SAP Central Finance, SAP Analytics Cloud, or SAP BTP.
CPA, CA, or equivalent professional accounting certification.
Experience working at a high-growth technology or SaaS company.
Prior experience working on SAP implementations.
Familiarity with NetSuite (helpful for understanding the current-state processes being migrated).
Experience with Databricks or other data platforms.
Public accounting experience (Big 4 or equivalent).
Why This Role
Shape SAP from day one — you are not inheriting a legacy system. You will define how SAP works for accounting at Databricks, with the authority to ensure it is built right the first time.
Challenge, don't just configure — this role exists specifically to push back on "that's how we've always done it" and ensure the implementation reflects what SAP can do, not what NetSuite did.
Own the platform long-term — this is not a project role. Post go-live, you will own continuous improvement, automation, and system operations — ensuring Databricks gets progressively more value from SAP over time.
Build on the Databricks platform — this is not a typical ERP role. You will define how SAP connects to the most advanced data and AI platform in the market, shaping how accounting data is used for reporting, analytics, and AI-driven automation. Few finance roles anywhere offer this combination.
Work at the intersection of accounting and technology — partner with a world-class finance team, a leading SI, and Databricks' own engineering organization to build something exceptional.
Grow your career — gain deep exposure to global accounting operations, finance transformation, and enterprise technology at one of the world's fastest-growing companies.

Production Solution Delivery: Deliver production-grade systems and reference architectures, contributing reusable frameworks, tools, and best practices along the way.

Own the Architecture: Contribute to architecture and design decisions for secure, scalable, full-stack solutions on the Databricks platform.

Collaborate closely with senior FDEs, Databricks engineering, and customer support to unblock customers and feed learnings back into the product.

Director of Engineering - Databricks Commercialization & Marketplace
P-1630
About the role
Every product Databricks ships has to be priced, contracted, rated and billed before it can earn a dollar. The Money organization builds the systems that make this happen, at hyperscaler scale and across every major cloud. We built the world's only cross-cloud integrated rating engine in-house, and it now rates billions of dollars in revenue. Our next goal is bigger: a fully automated, zero-touch order-to-cash flow where the platform is the source of truth for accounts, contracts and subscriptions, and Month End Close needs little or no human intervention.
As Director of Engineering, you will lead the engineering organization that owns this commercial engine from start to finish. You will set the product and technology strategy for how Databricks makes money. You will be the engineering voice Finance, Product and GTM leaders turn to for strategic decisions. You will also build the leadership bench that lets the organization keep scaling.
Speed is critical. Databricks keeps inventing new ways to sell: commit and pay-as-you-go, marketplaces, conditional benefits, strategic partnerships and new clouds and regions. The commerce engine either makes each of these fast and safe to launch, or it becomes the bottleneck. You will make sure it is the former.
What you'll own
The org covers six commercial domains:
Pricing configuration: SKUs, multipliers, price-change processes, deal desk and discounting
Orders and contracts: from negotiated quote to order to signed customer contract
Subscriptions: commit, pay-as-you-go and proof-of-concept subscriptions, plus how contracts are tied to payment methods
Rating: applying each customer's negotiated price, discounts and conditional benefits to ingested usage to compute the bill
Billing: commit drawdown, invoicing, Month End Close and related financial processes
Marketplace: third-party data and solutions, available seamlessly to Databricks customers
The impact you'll have
Set and communicate the vision. Write the multi-year product and technology strategy for the commerce engine, toward a zero-touch order-to-cash flow and a next-generation billing architecture. Present it clearly to executives, Finance and Product leaders, so that strategy and architecture decisions come to you by default.
Own business outcomes across orgs, not just your team's part. Revenue-critical programs routinely span 100+ people across Finance, Product, IT, Accounts and GTM. You will own the full outcome: dependency plans with clear owners, timelines, quality bars and escalation triggers, raised early in leadership forums so cross-org risks don't become executive surprises.
Make commercialization a platform capability. Build reusable building blocks (credits, commits, conditional benefits, marketplace and partner billing) so that new pricing models and routes to market ship in weeks, not quarters.
Treat foundations as seriously as features. Hold reliability, correctness, SOX and compliance readiness, security, cost visibility and operational load to the same standard as product launches. Billing errors should be structurally impossible, operational work should grow more slowly than revenue, and postmortems should actually lead to change.
Partner deeply with Business & Finance. Turn accounting, close and compliance requirements into engineering design. Keep improving the Month End Close timeline and audit readiness, and earn the trust of Technical Accounting, Revenue Ops and Strategy & Execution leaders.
Build a team of leaders. Grow the organization from one with a large group of direct-report engineers to one led by strong engineering managers and tech-lead managers, with clear subteams, domain boundaries and named owners. Coach managers to be great people leaders, give specific feedback and career plans, and recognize high-performing teams publicly.
Hire like a founder. Act as the hiring owner for the Money Bellevue site. Source and close senior engineering and management talent, put the company first when placing hires across Money teams, and help raise the Databricks engineering hiring bar.
What we're looking for
12+ years in software engineering, including 6+ years leading engineering organizations and managing managers, ideally in billing, payments, commerce, fintech or other systems where errors directly cost revenue or create regulatory exposure
A track record of delivering large, revenue-critical, cross-functional programs (for example, replacing a billing or rating system, migrating a source of truth, or automating order-to-cash) on time and with high quality
Technical depth in distributed systems and large-scale data pipelines. You can discuss correctness, idempotency, reconciliation and data lineage with tech leads, and you know when to coach and when to decide.
Fluency in order-to-cash and finance concepts: pricing and discounting, contracts, revenue recognition, invoicing, month-end close, SOX controls. You have earned trust as a partner to Finance and Accounting leaders.
Strong product judgment: you can spot gaps in the commercial platform, shape requirements with Product, and make build-versus-buy decisions that pay off over time
Clear, confident communication of strategy to executives, plus the ability to influence peers in Product, Finance, IT and GTM without direct authority
Experience scaling an organization quickly while keeping a high hiring bar, developing strong leaders and engineers, and keeping them engaged on internal platform work
BS in Computer Science or a related field; MS preferred. Experience with Kafka, Apache Spark, Delta Lake or cloud (AWS, Azure, GCP) is a plus.
Why this role
You will run the engine behind the revenue of one of the fastest-growing data and AI companies in the world. The problems involve hard distributed-systems correctness at scale, high financial and compliance stakes, and a direct, visible link to company growth. You'll lead an established, high-trust team with a strong delivery record and help shape what the next generation of the commerce engine looks like.

As the Director of Technical Marketing at Databricks, you will lead and scale the team responsible for explaining Databricks products, and what you can do with them, at scale to technical buyers and practitioners (from data engineers, data scientists, and ML engineers to solutions architects, platform teams, security engineers, and application developers). You will own the strategy and execution of technical content in written and video form, demos, workshops, launch storytelling, and outbound evangelism that drives technical mindshare, consideration, product adoption, and ultimately pipeline. In the era of agentic marketing and AEO/GEO, your team will increasingly produce content designed to educate both humans and agents alike. You will also play an outsized role in programming the technical content for key Databricks events, such as the Data + AI Summit and Data + AI World Tour, among others. Reporting to the SVP of Product & Solutions Marketing, you will manage a team of 6+ Technical Marketing Managers (growing) and serve as the connective tissue between Product, Product Marketing, Field Engineering, and the broader technical community.
This role expands the traditional TMM charter to include a stronger outbound evangelism dimension, becoming a visible, trusted technical voice externally through social media, YouTube, conferences, and the data practitioner ecosystem while continuing to own the core technical content engine that powers Summit, World Tour, workshops, and field enablement.
The impact you will have:
First 6 months:
Assess the current TMM team's strengths, gaps, and capacity; establish a clear operating model with defined ownership areas (product coverage, content types, GEO) and a quarterly planning cadence.
Own and deliver the technical content agenda for Data + AI World Tour and/or the next major Tier 1 event, achieving ≥4.5/5.0 average session ratings and measurable pipeline contribution.
Launch or significantly expand at least 2 new outbound evangelism motions (e.g., a YouTube series architecture, a technical social media cadence, or a creator/influencer engagement program) that grow Databricks' external technical reach by ≥25%.
Build an AI-powered publishing engine that enables the TMM team to scale content faster, leveraging AI assistance for content creation and publishing.
Establish yourself as a credible external technical voice, publishing 3+ original technical pieces (blogs, videos, or talks) and representing Databricks at 2+ external events or podcasts.
First 12 months:
Scale the TMM team to meet growing demand across an expanding set of technical personas (solutions architects, platform engineers, security teams, data scientists, analysts, app developers) driven by the 2026+ product surface (Lakebase, Genie, Lakewatch, Agent Bricks, Omnigent).
Work with Databricks Field Engineering and FDE (Forward-Deployed Engineering) to capture repeatable product use cases into a Solutions Library, building a motion to scale capture and marketing of these use cases for learning across the entire community.
Build and operationalize a "1 launch → many assets" content engine that converts every major product launch into persona-specific learning journeys (demos, workshops, blogs, videos, social).
Grow Databricks' YouTube and social technical content reach by 2x, with a series-based content architecture targeting key personas at multiple depth levels.
Drive measurable contribution to AEO/GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) ensuring Databricks is cited by default in AI answer engines for key buyer questions.
First 18–24 months:
Establish Databricks as the default place every technical practitioner learns data + AI, measured by YouTube subscriber growth (target: 300K+), technical content engagement, and Free Edition activation rates tied to content.
Build a formal Databricks Creators program that turns independent creator reach into co-owned, accurate, early-access content across new product areas.
Develop the TMM team into a recognized center of excellence — with clear career paths, a strong hiring bar, and a reputation as one of the best technical marketing teams in enterprise software.
What we look for:
10+ years of experience in technical marketing, developer relations, solutions engineering, field engineering, or a related technical field in enterprise software / SaaS / cloud.
3+ years of people management experience, with a track record of hiring, developing, and retaining high-performing technical teams.
Deep technical fluency in data, AI/ML, and cloud platforms, comfortable building demos and engaging credibly with data engineers, data scientists, solutions architects, and other technical practitioners across the data + AI ecosystem.
Demonstrated outbound evangelism skills, including a visible external presence through conference speaking, technical blogging, YouTube/video content, or social media thought leadership.
Experience owning technical content strategy for major product launches and flagship events (e.g., user conferences, world tours).
Strong cross-functional influence with a proven ability to partner with Product Management, Product Marketing, Field Engineering, and Sales to align on priorities and deliver integrated GTM.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex technical concepts into compelling narratives for multiple audiences.
Preferred:
Experience with data platforms, lakehouse architectures, Apache Spark, or related open-source data technologies.
Experience building or scaling a YouTube channel, podcast, or technical content program for practitioner audiences.
Familiarity with GEO / AI answer engine optimization strategies.
Experience with technical community building, creator programs, or influencer engagement across practitioner audiences.
Track record of building technical content that drives measurable pipeline and product adoption.

RDQ427R123
At Databricks, we are passionate about enabling data teams to solve the world's toughest problems — from making the next mode of transportation a reality to accelerating the development of medical breakthroughs. We do this by building and running the world's best data and AI infrastructure platform so our customers can use deep data insights to improve their business. Founded by engineers — and customer obsessed — we leap at every opportunity to tackle technical challenges, from designing next-gen UI/UX for interfacing with data to scaling our services and infrastructure across millions of virtual machines. And we're only getting started.
Databricks is looking for an Engineering Manager to lead the App Traffic team, responsible for critical networking infrastructure that powers communication across the Databricks platform. The team builds and operates Databricks’ unified service mesh, including ingress, service discovery, service-to-service communication, traffic management, and intelligent routing across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud. Lakebase Associate Director, Healthcare & Life Sciences
Databricks is seeking a Lakebase Associate Sales Director to help healthcare & life sciences customers modernize their operational data foundation with Databricks Lakebase, our fully-managed Postgres offering for intelligent applications. This high-impact role sits within the Lakebase Go-To-Market team and partners closely with regional Account Executives to drive adoption of Lakebase with platform, application, and data teams.
Lakebase gives customers a unified, governed foundation for operational workloads and AI-native applications, helping them move away from a fragmented estate of point databases toward a modern, scalable, serverless Postgres service. If you want to be at the forefront of operational databases for AI and intelligent applications at one of the fastest-growing data and AI companies in the world, this is your opportunity.
The impact you will have:
Drive new Lakebase revenue by identifying, qualifying, and driving Lakebase activations and consumption within a defined territory, in partnership with regional Account Executives and the broader account team.
Lead with outcomes for key Lakebase personas — including platform teams and developers, data teams, and central IT — articulating how Lakebase helps them ship features faster, simplify operational data architectures, and improve governance and cost efficiency.
Sell the value of fully-managed Postgres for intelligent applications , positioning Lakebase as the optimal choice for operational workloads that power real-time, AI-driven experiences.
Run complex, multi-threaded sales cycles from discovery and value hypothesis through commercial negotiation and close, navigating executive, technical, and line-of-business stakeholders.
Orchestrate proof-of-value and POCs that validate Lakebase’s benefits for OLTP-style workloads, reverse ETL, and AI/ML-driven applications, in partnership with solution architects and specialists.
Compete and win against legacy and cloud-native operational databases by leveraging our compete assets, benchmarks, and customer references.
Align to measurable business outcomes such as performance, developer productivity, time-to-market for new features, cost reduction, and simplification of the operational data landscape.
Partner cross-functionally with Product Management, Marketing, Customer Success, and Partner teams to shape territory plans, launch plays, and co-selling motions with key ISVs and GSIs.
Enable the field by sharing Lakebase best practices, success stories, and sales motions with broader sales teams, helping scale Lakebase proficiency across the organization.
What success looks like in this role:
This role requires the ability to operate across two key motions simultaneously:
Establish top strategic focus accounts by engaging application development teams to create net-new intelligent applications leveraging Lakebase.
Drive longer-term Postgres standardization and migration within Databricks' most strategic accounts.
Candidates should demonstrate how they can act as a force multiplier across multiple dimensions of the business.
Success in this role requires strength in four areas:
Business ownership – Operate at a business-unit level by tracking revenue, pipeline, and key observations, and by identifying areas needing additional focus or support.
Strategic account engagement – Partner with account teams to engage priority accounts across the global DB700, driving strategic opportunities from initial engagement through successful outcomes.
Field, account, & customer enablement: Align customers and the field on the value of Lakebase by equipping AEs and SAs with the messaging and execution motions needed to confidently own accounts without specialist intervention.
Market voice and thought leadership – Develop an internal and external presence by contributing to global AMAs and internal forums, and by representing Databricks at key first- and third-party events.
What we look for
7+ years of enterprise SaaS sales experience, consistently exceeding quota in complex, multi-stakeholder deals.
Proven success selling data platforms, operational databases (e.g., Postgres, MySQL, cloud-native DBaaS), or adjacent data/AI infrastructure to technical buyers and business leaders.
Strong understanding of modern data and application architectures, including cloud-native services, microservices, event-driven systems, and how operational data underpins AI and analytics strategies.
Ability to sell to both technical stakeholders (developers, architects, data engineers) and business stakeholders (product leaders, operations, line-of-business owners).
Demonstrated experience leading specialist or overlay motions, working jointly with core Account Executives to create and progress opportunities.
Executive presence with the ability to whiteboard architectures, lead C-level conversations, and build trust with senior decision makers.
Strong value selling skills: adept at discovering pain, building a business case, and tying technical capabilities to clear, quantified outcomes.
Excellent communication, storytelling, and negotiation skills, with comfort presenting to both large and small audiences.
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience.
Preferred qualifications
Experience selling Postgres, operational databases, OLTP workloads, or transactional cloud database services, ideally within large or strategic accounts.
Familiarity with data platforms, lakehouse architectures, and cloud ecosystems (AWS, Azure, GCP), including how operational databases fit within broader data and AI strategies.
Understanding of reverse ETL, real-time decisioning, and operational analytics use cases, and how they drive value for customer-facing and internal applications.
Exposure to AI-native and agent-driven applications that depend on low-latency, highly scalable operational data services.
Prior experience in a high-growth, category-creating environment, helping shape new plays, messaging, and customer narratives.
Experience collaborating with partners and ISVs to drive joint pipeline and co-sell motions.

At Databricks, we are passionate about enabling data teams to solve the world's most challenging problems — from making the next mode of transportation a reality to accelerating medical breakthroughs. We do this by building and running the world's best data and AI platform, enabling our customers to use deep data insights to improve their businesses. Our ability to execute this mission depends on building trust and recognition within an ever-growing community of data engineers, analysts, scientists, machine learning practitioners, and AI practitioners.
Databricks’ Developer Relations team is looking for a leader to manage our open source Developer Advocates, deepen our engagement across the Apache Software Foundation and Linux Foundation communities, and lead technical storytelling and experiences that strengthen trust and adoption. This role is ideal for someone who thrives in the spotlight, is known and respected in open source communities, and gets even more satisfaction from growing other advocates than from giving the keynote themselves.
As the Developer Advocate Manager for Open Source, you'll lead the team that advocates for the projects Databricks builds in the open, and serve as a crucial link between our engineering teams and the global community of practitioners building their careers on them. Your team's remit spans the Open Lakehouse — Apache Spark™ (including Spark Declarative Pipelines), Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, Apache Iceberg™, and MLflow — as well as Omnigent, our open source meta-harness for composing, governing, and sharing AI agents. As the original creators of Apache Spark™, Delta Lake, and MLflow, we hold ourselves to a high standard here: our credibility in these communities is earned continuously, not inherited.
This role will leverage your expertise in building and scaling a developer relations team, and it will build on your standing within the open source world and your working relationships with the Apache Software Foundation, the Linux Foundation, and the maintainers and committers who keep these projects healthy. You'll coach your team on building a content flywheel — where a single demo, video, or talk becomes the source of truth for a dozen derivative assets — and on applying AI as a force multiplier without ever lowering the technical bar.
Your responsibilities will encompass both team leadership and a wide range of knowledge-sharing activities. You'll lead by example: delivering engaging talks, hosting panels and meetups, creating blogs and video content, developing courseware, answering questions in community forums, and meeting one-on-one with influential contributors and maintainers.
Community engagement will be at the heart of your role. You'll work closely with the open source communities and with product and engineering teams, ensuring that community needs and product development align seamlessly. Reporting directly to the Head of Developer Relations, you'll collaborate with fellow DevRel managers across our Databricks, App Dev, and DevRel Programs teams to create a cohesive and impactful open source strategy.

Our ability to execute this mission depends on building trust and recognition within an ever-growing community of data engineers, analysts, scientists, machine learning practitioners, and AI practitioners.
Databricks’ Developer Relations team is looking for a leader to manage our open source Developer Advocates, deepen our engagement across the Apache Software Foundation and Linux Foundation communities, and lead technical storytelling and experiences that strengthen trust and adoption. This role is ideal for someone who thrives in the spotlight, is known and respected in open source communities, and gets even more satisfaction from growing other advocates than from giving the keynote themselves.
As the Developer Advocate Manager for Open Source, you'll lead the team that advocates for the projects Databricks builds in the open, and serve as a crucial link between our engineering teams and the global community of practitioners building their careers on them. Your team's remit spans the Open Lakehouse — Apache Spark™ (including Spark Declarative Pipelines), Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, Apache Iceberg™, and MLflow — as well as Omnigent, our open source meta-harness for composing, governing, and sharing AI agents. GAQ126R43
About Databricks
At Databricks, our mission is to help data teams solve the world's toughest problems—and that begins with empowering our own employees with exceptional internal products. The Databricks IT organization is a product-led engineering team building intelligent, AI-powered platforms that simplify how work gets done across the company. For Finance, our vision is to eliminate manual, repetitive work by automating complex business processes, surfacing actionable insights, and orchestrating end-to-end workflows. We are reimagining finance operations so teams spend less time processing transactions, chasing approvals, and resolving exceptions, and more time delivering strategic insights that accelerate the business.
We're looking for an SAP Technical Lead to own the technical architecture and delivery of our SAP platform. In this role, you'll define the technical vision for a clean-core S/4HANA landscape, lead the engineers who build on it, and architect the intelligent, agentic AI layer that sits between SAP and the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform. You'll set the standards, make the hard build-versus-adopt calls, and ensure everything we ship is secure, performant, and built to scale.
The Opportunity
SAP will serve as the foundation for Databricks' core finance processes, including Record-to-Report, Source-to-Pay, and Order-to-Cash. As the SAP Technical Lead, you will own how those processes are engineered—from the clean-core S/4HANA core and its extensions, to the integration fabric that connects SAP to the rest of the enterprise, to the AI and agentic services that make the experience intelligent. Rather than accumulating custom code inside the digital core, you'll champion a modern extensibility model on SAP BTP and the Databricks Lakehouse, so Finance teams get automated, AI-driven workflows on top of a core that stays clean, upgradable, and fast. Your mission is to combine the strength of SAP with the power of Databricks AI to build a technical foundation that lets the business scale.
What You'll Do
Own the Technical Architecture: Define and own the end-to-end technical architecture for the S/4HANA landscape (greenfield, brownfield, or selective data transition), aligned to clean-core principles, with clear guardrails that keep the digital core standard and upgrade-ready.
Lead the Extensibility Strategy: Define and own the extensibility strategy for SAP, using Databricks-native applications to address business requirements beyond core SAP capabilities. Establish clear architecture and governance standards to ensure extensions are scalable, secure, and aligned with the broader Finance technology strategy.
Drive Enterprise AI Integration: Drive a strong integration with ongoing Enterprise AI transformation within Databricks by bringing AI fluency and hands on AI experience.
Design the Integration Fabric: Architect secure, resilient integration across SAP and non-SAP systems using SAP Integration Suite, event-driven patterns, APIs, OData v4, and change-data feeds into the Lakehouse, with clear contracts, error handling, and observability.
Unify SAP Data in the Lakehouse: Partner with data engineering on the technical patterns for landing SAP data in Databricks—ingestion, CDC, semantic and master-data modeling, lineage, and governance.
Set Engineering Standards: Establish CI/CD, automated testing, and transport/deployment pipelines for BTP artifacts; own code and design reviews; and define the technical standards, security patterns, and best practices the team builds against.
Lead the Team: Mentor developers and architects, lead technical steering, and act as the connective tissue across the SAP ecosystem (BTP, Integration Suite) and the systems around it, partnering closely with functional, product, and partner engineering teams.
Be Accountable for Non-Functionals: Own performance, scalability, security, resilience, and cost across the landscape; report technical status, risks, and roadmaps to stakeholders.
What You Bring
10+ years in SAP technical roles , with 3+ years as a technical lead or architect, and a proven track record delivering at least one full S/4HANA program (greenfield or conversion) plus BTP-based extension delivery.
Clean-Core Architecture: Deep, hands-on command of clean-core principles—custom-code assessment and remediation, in-app vs. side-by-side extensibility, released APIs and extension points, and the governance that keeps the core clean over time.
SAP BTP & Modern Development: Advanced experience across SAP BTP, ABAP Cloud and the ABAP RESTful Application Programming Model (RAP), CDS, and CAP, with Fiori/SAPUI5 on the front end.
AI & Agentic Systems: Hands-on experience or strong technical command of agentic automation, LLM orchestration, retrieval-augmented generation, and evaluation—plus clear judgment about where AI belongs in a controlled, auditable ERP process and where it does not.
Integration & APIs: Advanced experience with SAP Integration Suite, API management, event-driven architecture, and REST/OData, integrating hybrid SAP and non-SAP landscapes.
Data Fluency: Solid understanding of modern data platforms, SAP data extraction and modeling, pipelines, and semantic layers, and the practical work of making ERP data usable for analytics and AI.
Governance Rigor: Working knowledge of SAP authorizations, SoD, SOX and audit requirements, and the ability to architect solutions and automation that satisfy them.
Leadership: Ability to translate business requirements into technical architecture, present tradeoffs to non-technical stakeholders, mentor engineers, and make pragmatic decisions that balance speed against long-term maintainability.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience building custom applications or automation layers on modern data platforms (such as Databricks) that extend or sit alongside SAP.
A clear point of view on build-versus-adopt tradeoffs across the SAP AI and extension stack (BTP, AI Core, Joule) versus a Databricks-native approach.
Hands-on knowledge of SAP integration surfaces and their limitations, including OData and REST APIs, CDS views, and Datasphere.
Experience running Agile delivery with system integrators and managed service partners, including vendor and SLA accountability.
SAP certification in SAP BTP, S/4HANA, or a relevant technology area, and prior work in a high-growth technology company where ERP had to scale quickly.

The Self-Serve team owns Databricks' product-led growth motion — the experience that takes someone from "I just heard about Databricks" to succeeding on the platform entirely on their own. Our most ambitious bet is Learning: making Databricks the place where anyone interested in data + AI comes to learn, and building the largest community of active, capable learners in the world. It's a long game with a simple thesis — if people learn data + AI on Databricks, it becomes ubiquitous with the field itself, driving adoption and revenue.
As a Senior Engineering Manager on the Self-Serve team, you will lead the Learning bet end to end across two sides: self-paced learning — a place to learn any Databricks skill, hands-on labs that spin up inside a real workspace, and a durable skill profile a learner carries across jobs — and enterprise-managed learning, giving admins the tools to assign, track, and grow learning inside their orgs. AI is central to both: a content-generation agent that scales the catalog far past what we could author by hand, and an AI tutor that guides learners hands-on inside the product. This is a genuine 0→1 product with real systems depth — on-demand provisioning, identity, sandboxing, and an interactive learning engine that must scale to millions of learners — and you'll grow and lead a team of ~12 engineers (planned to roughly double) to build it.

Strategy & Vision: Define and drive the technical and product strategy for Learning, and tie it into the broader self-serve growth motion.

Databricks is looking for a strategic compensation leader who likes to build. You'll be a trusted partner to founders and senior leaders in our Engineering organization. Together you'll create compensation solutions that help us attract, retain and motivate world-class engineering and technical talent, and you'll use AI to build the tools that make those solutions scale. This role reports to the Director of Compensation.
At Databricks, compensation is more than a number. It's how we show that every employee is an owner and part of our success. We're looking for someone with a strong foundation and a track record of doing exactly that.
What it takes to thrive
Databricks is a deeply technical, fast-moving company, and our Engineering organization builds the platform everything else runs on. You'll partner with highly technical, data-driven leaders who expect rigorous analysis, clear points of view and collaborative problem-solving. Priorities can change quickly, and you'll often run several important initiatives at once.
We set high standards for this role to support our fast-paced growth. Successful team members in this environment tend to:
Build trust through analytical rigor. You present well-reasoned models and effectively articulate complex analysis to engineering leaders who will test your assumptions.
Navigate fast-paced priorities with resilience. You maintain focus, sound judgment, and positivity when balancing competing deadlines and feedback.
Offer constructive perspectives. You confidently partner with senior stakeholders to propose data-backed alternative solutions and drive alignment to finalize decisions.
Embrace feedback as a growth tool. You extract actionable insights from feedback and respond with clarity and openness.
Create order from ambiguity. When there's no playbook, you build one, and you're comfortable acting on 80% of the information.
If you are excited by high standards, technical depth, and collaborative strategic discussions, you will find this work deeply rewarding.
The impact you will have
This is a hands-on, high-impact role. Expected time on each area:
Engineering compensation solutions and strategic advice (40%)
Work directly with Engineering leaders to diagnose talent challenges, such as competition for AI/ML and infrastructure talent, hard-to-fill specialist roles, rapid team scaling, acquisitions and reorganizations. Then design attraction and retention solutions that solve them.
Turn vague or urgent requests into clear options with explicit tradeoffs, and help leaders reach a decision.
Serve as the main compensation advisor on strategic technical hires (senior ICs, distinguished engineers, research leaders and engineering executives) and on high-stakes retention cases.
Advise on technical leveling, including IC and management career paths and how compensation should differ across them.
AI-enabled lifecycle compensation (30%)
Run merit, refresh equity and promotion cycles end to end for global R&D teams.
Design and build AI tools and workflows that reduce manual work and improve decisions. Examples include offer modeling, retention-risk analysis, cycle quality checks, and self-serve insights for leaders.
Spot what's repetitive or error-prone in today's processes and automate it.
Enterprise compensation frameworks (30%)
Help scale Databricks' global compensation structure, including market pricing models, pay-for-performance design, equity strategy and technical job architecture.
Build frameworks that solve today's problems and anticipate the ones coming as we grow, including emerging skill premiums such as AI/ML.
What we look for
Quantitative and technical skill is the foundation of this role. Everything else we look for builds on it.
1. Quantitative and technical foundation (required)
Expert-level analytical modeling. You build compensation models from scratch, including cost-of-program scenarios, pay-positioning analysis, attrition and retention-risk modeling, and sensitivity and tradeoff analysis.
Built with AI. You've personally used AI tools (for example LLMs, AI assistants, or automation and agent platforms) to build compensation tools, models or workflows that others rely on. You don't need to be a software engineer, but you should be able to explain how it works, what you'd improve, and how you checked that its outputs were accurate.
Equity fluency. You understand RSU and option mechanics, vesting design, refresh strategy, and how grant values and share price movement affect cost and retention, especially for long-tenured, high-equity technical talent.
Statistical judgment. You know when a market data cut is credible, when a sample is too small (common with niche technical roles), and how to present ranges and market pricing without false precision.
2. Compensation expertise (required)
You know your craft. Job architecture, technical career ladders, compensation frameworks, market pricing, year-end and mid-year pay cycles, global compensation practices, and pay-for-performance design.
You know the competition. Deep knowledge of competitor compensation for high-tech talent, especially new-hire and refresh equity strategy at high-growth tech companies, public tech companies, and AI labs.
You reason from first principles. You balance compensation best practice with what the business actually needs, and you can rebuild a framework from its underlying logic when the standard approach doesn't fit.
3. Strategic partnership (required)
Trusted advisor to senior leaders. You have a track record of advising executives on sensitive, high-stakes compensation decisions (offers, promotions, leveling, retention, transfers, org changes) and influencing the outcome through data and judgment rather than authority.
Operational excellence. You connect the dots between systems, stakeholders and programs to deliver compensation programs end to end, accurately and on time.
Clear communicator. You turn complex analysis into a crisp recommendation an executive can act on in one conversation.
Nice-to-haves
Experience supporting Engineering, R&D or other technical organizations at a high-growth tech company.
Familiarity with the market for AI/ML, research or specialized infrastructure talent.
Experience with acquisition (including acqui-hire) compensation and retention design.
Experience with Tableau or other BI tools, or building dashboards for leaders.
Experience scaling compensation programs through hypergrowth, IPO, or major organizational change.
A background in a quantitative field (for example finance, statistics, engineering), or equivalent experience.

At Databricks, we run the world's largest AI platform. We believe the next breakthroughs will come from models trained on domain-specific enterprise data, not from bigger general-purpose models alone.
That's why we built AI Runtime , a serverless product that makes GPU training of any size feel simple, so companies can train their own models the way frontier labs do. Customers across industries train on it, right next to the enterprise data already in Databricks. Among them are Rivian in automotive, Robinhood in fintech, and Merck, which builds foundation models for drug discovery. Our own AI researchers use it to post-train models with hundreds of billions to nearly a trillion parameters.
It takes a lot of engineering to make that work, and we've written about it on our blog: how we keep GPUs reliable , make training fault-tolerant , and speed up fine-tuning with fused kernels and smart sequence packing. AI agents now launch experiments too, and on our research team they've already increased training jobs 8x .
As a Senior Software Engineer, you'll work on the systems behind all of this, solving hard technical problems and helping shape how AI Runtime evolves.
The impact you will have:
Build core parts of AI Runtime and contribute to Databricks' technical direction in AI training infrastructure.
Develop reliability and observability features for a fleet that keeps growing in scale and complexity.
Improve AI Runtime's developer experience for people and agents, so even the largest training jobs feel as simple as a first experiment.
Help prepare AI Runtime for new GPU generations and workload types.
Take on hard multi-node training problems, from orchestration and GPU scheduling to data loading and checkpointing.
Make training faster and cheaper by raising efficiency across model architectures and GPU accelerators.
Work with research, product, and customers on what we build next and own features from design through production.
Champion engineering excellence, raise the bar, and help the engineers around you grow.
What we look for:
5+ years in large-scale distributed systems, with experience in GPU training, high-performance computing, or ML systems.
Experience training large models with FSDP, DeepSpeed, or Megatron, and familiarity with parallelism strategies.
Working knowledge of GPU performance, including accelerator architecture, high-speed interconnects, and kernels.
Strong understanding of training resilience patterns, such as checkpointing, failure detection, and automatic recovery.
A background in building and running multi-tenant cloud platforms as products.
A track record of owning complex features end to end and seeing them through to customer impact.
The clarity to explain technical designs in writing and in person, and a reputation as a teammate others learn from.
BS in Computer Science or a related field (MS or PhD preferred).

At Databricks, we are passionate about enabling data teams to solve the world’s toughest problems, from advancing AI research to powering next-generation applications. We do this by building and operating the world’s best data and AI infrastructure platform. Founded by engineers and driven by customer obsession, we embrace the hardest technical challenges, whether it’s scaling distributed systems across multiple clouds or delivering reliable, low-latency communication between thousands of services. And we’re only getting started.
As a Senior Software Engineer on the Application Traffic team , you will design and build the systems that power Databricks’ service-to-service communication across thousands of clusters in a multi-cloud environment. You will also help create abstractions that hide networking complexity from product teams, making connectivity, discovery, and reliability seamless by default.
The impact you’ll have:
You’ll work across three key areas that define Databricks’ networking stack:
Ingress Control Plane : Build the control plane for Databricks’ global ingress layer. Enable programming of API gateways with static and dynamic endpoints, simplify service onboarding, and make it easy to expose APIs securely across clouds.
Service-to-Service Communication : Design scalable mechanisms for service discovery and load balancing across thousands of clusters. Provide networking abstractions so product teams don’t need to worry about underlying connectivity details.
Overload Protection : Build intelligent rate limiting and admission control systems to protect critical services under high load. Ensure reliability and predictable performance for both customer-facing and internal workloads.
What we look for:
BS (or higher) in Computer Science or related field
5+ years of experience designing and building large-scale distributed systems
Strong proficiency in one or more languages such as Java, Scala, Go, or C++
Experience with service-oriented architectures and large scale distributed systems
Familiarity with cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP) and container/orchestration technologies (Kubernetes, Docker)
Track record of shipping infrastructure that supports mission-critical workloads at scale

The Opportunity
Multi-cloud is core to Databricks product strategy. Compute serves as the layer that abstracts the cloud from the rest of the company. Building unified infrastructure on top of heterogeneous clouds is a challenge that few companies experience.
As an engineer on this team, you won’t just manage infrastructure; you will build it as a product. You will tackle the hard problems of distributed systems: sub-second container/MicroVM startup times, multi-tenant security isolation, and building a unified orchestration layer that scales across AWS, Azure, and GCP.
What You’ll Do
Design and build the next generation of our Serverless platform, focusing on high availability, low latency, and scale-to-zero efficiency.
Build a single compute stack that supports heterogeneous workloads, including GPU instance qualification for AI training and stateful execution for Lakebase.
Solve Multi-Cloud Complexity: Develop platform-level abstractions that allow Databricks to run seamlessly across all major cloud providers.
Optimize everything from the API gateway down to the host-level networking and container orchestration.
Work alongside industry experts who have built world-class systems like Borg, Kubernetes, and Uber’s infrastructure.
What We’re Looking For
5+ years of production-level experience in one of: Python, Java, Scala, C++, or a similar language
4+ years of experience developing large-scale distributed systems from scratch
Experience with Kubernetes, Docker, or MicroVM technologies (e.g., Firecracker) and a strong grasp of cloud provider internals (AWS/Azure/GCP).
You aren't just a user of tools; you understand how to build them from the ground up when existing solutions fail at our scale.

Our mission at Databricks is to radically simplify the whole data lifecycle from ingestion to ETL, BI, and all the way up to ML/AI with a unified platform. To achieve this goal, we believe the data warehouse architecture as we know it today will be replaced by a new architectural pattern, Lakehouse ( CIDR 2021 paper ), open platforms that unify data warehousing and advanced analytics. The new architecture will help address several major challenges, including data staleness, reliability, total cost of ownership, data lock-in, and limited use-case support.
A critical part of realizing this vision is the next generation (decoupled) query engine and structured storage system that can outperform specialized data warehouses in relational query performance, yet retain the expressiveness and of general purpose systems such as Apache Spark™ to support diverse workloads ranging from ETL to data science.
As part of this team, you will be working in one or more of the following areas to design and implement these next gen systems that leapfrog state-of-the-art:
Query compilation and optimization
Distributed query execution and scheduling
Vectorized execution engine
Data security
Resource management
Transaction coordination
Efficient storage structures (encodings, indexes)
Automatic physical data optimization
What we look for:
A passion for database systems, storage systems, distributed systems, language design, or performance optimization
Experience working towards a multi-year vision with incremental deliverables
Motivated by delivering customer value and impact
5+ years of experience working in a related system (preferred)
Optional: PhD in databases or distributed systems

The Digital Employee Experience team builds the internal tools, platforms, and data systems that power how every Brickser works. From procurement applications and SaaS inventory systems to mobile apps, AI-powered tools, and data pipelines that serve IT.
As a Senior Software Engineer on this team, you will own projects end-to-end and be the team lead of software engineers. You will own architecture, design, implementation, deployment, and stakeholder management. You'll build production web and mobile applications on the Databricks Platform, design data pipelines that ingest from dozens of SaaS systems, and ship AI-powered integrations (MCP servers, LLM features) that reduce friction across the entire company. This is a high-autonomy, high-impact role where you operate with a startup mentality inside a scaled organization.
The impact you will have
Design, build, and maintain production full-stack applications (web and mobile) used company-wide. Such as, but not limited to, procurement platforms, employee experience apps, SaaS management tools, and mobile apps for leadership.
Build and own data pipelines that ingest, transform, and serve data from SaaS systems into Databricks, ensuring data quality and pipeline reliability.
Architect and implement authentication and authorization flows using Okta, OAuth, and service principals.
Build and deploy MCPs that connect internal tools to AI assistants, and contribute to AI-powered features, including LLM-based classification, data enrichment, and prompt-based guardrails.
Design and manage CI/CD pipelines, Infrastructure as Code, and deployment automation using GitHub, HashiCorp Vault, and Databricks tooling.
Improve and enforce SWE standards for the team: PR review processes, testing frameworks, and environment management (dev/staging/prod).
Work directly with stakeholders across Security, Legal, HR, Finance, and Engineering to gather requirements, navigate trade-offs, and deliver solutions.
Author design documents, PRDs, and architecture proposals for new systems and features.
Mentor contractors and junior engineers. Delegate work, break down roadmap items, and drive project planning with minimal management oversight.
Drive roadmap planning for your domain by identifying high-impact work and autonomously sequencing it.
What we look for
Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field.
5+ years of production software development experience, with demonstrated full-stack proficiency (backend, frontend, and data).
Strong experience with Python as a primary language, with production experience building full-stack applications.
Experience designing and deploying applications on cloud platforms (AWS and/or Azure).
Hands-on experience with data engineering — building ETL/ELT pipelines, working with structured and semi-structured data.
Familiarity with CI/CD, IaC, and modern DevOps practices (GitHub Actions, Terraform, Docker).
Experience with SaaS platforms or service-oriented architectures.
Experience with security and systems that handle sensitive data: identity management, access control, RBAC/RLS patterns.
Strong communication skills. You can write a clear design doc, present to cross-functional stakeholders, and navigate technical trade-offs with non-technical audiences.
Experience with AI/ML tooling, LLM integrations, prompt engineering, evals, and MCP servers.
Experience mentoring other engineers.
Bonus points
Experience with the Databricks platform (Unity Catalog, Delta Lake, Databricks Apps, Workflows).
Strong SQL proficiency.
Familiarity with identity and access management systems (Okta, Opal, Google Workspace).
Experience building mobile applications (iOS/Android).
Experience with SaaS management, procurement systems, or IT operations tooling.
Background in data governance, schema design, access control, and data quality monitoring.
Experience working with distributed teams across time zones.

At Databricks, we are passionate about enabling data teams to solve the world's toughest problems — from making the next mode of transportation a reality to accelerating the development of medical breakthroughs. We do this by building and running the world's best data and AI infrastructure platform so our customers can use deep data insights to improve their business. Founded by engineers — and customer obsessed — we leap at every opportunity to solve technical challenges, from designing next-gen UI/UX for interfacing with data to scaling our services and infrastructure across millions of virtual machines. And we're only getting started.
Modern data analysis employs sophisticated methods such as machine learning that go well beyond the roll-up and drill-down capabilities of traditional SQL query engines. As a software engineer on the Runtime team at Databricks, you will be building the next generation distributed data storage and processing systems that can outperform specialized SQL query engines in relational query performance, yet provide the expressiveness and programming abstractions to support diverse workloads ranging from ETL to data science.
Below are some example projects:
Apache Spark™ : Develop the de facto open source standard framework for big data.
Data Plane Storage : Provide reliable and high performance services and client libraries for storing and accessing humongous amount of data on cloud storage backends, e.g., AWS S3, Azure Blob Store.
Delta Lake : A storage management system that combines the scale and cost-efficiency of data lakes, the performance and reliability of a data warehouse, and the low latency of streaming. Its higher level abstractions and guarantees, including ACID transactions and time travel, drastically simplify the complexity of real-world data engineering architecture.
Delta Pipelines : It's difficult to manage even a single data engineering pipeline. The goal of the Delta Pipelines project is to make it simple and possible to orchestrate and operate tens of thousands of data pipelines. It provides a higher level abstraction for expressing data pipelines and enables customers to deploy, test & upgrade pipelines and eliminate operational burdens for managing and building high quality data pipelines.
Performance Engineering : Build the next generation query optimizer and execution engine that's fast, tuning free, scalable, and robust.
What we look for:
BS (or higher) in Computer Science, related technical field or equivalent practical experience.
Comfortable working towards a multi-year vision with incremental deliverables.
Motivated by delivering customer value and impact.
5+ years of production level experience in either Java, Scala or C++.
Strong foundation in algorithms and data structures and their real-world use cases.
Experience with distributed systems, databases, and big data systems (Apache Spark™, Hadoop).

Who We Are
Our GenAI observability and quality product provides advanced monitoring and insights for GenAI systems, giving customers real-time visibility into their system's performance, along with a suite of tools to improve the quality of the GenAI systems. With features like real-time alerts, detailed logging, and anomaly detection, customers can quickly identify and fix issues that affect the quality of their GenAI systems. This is a great opportunity to use next-gen tools for continuous monitoring, testing, and feedback, while applying cutting-edge technologies like AutoML/AutoRag, LLM fine-tuning, Prompt Optimization and Automation to improve the performance and quality of GenAI systems.
We are looking for a passionate and experienced Senior Full-Stack Software Engineer to join our dynamic team. This role will offer you the opportunity to contribute to both the front-end and back-end development of our product, while also allowing you to bring your strong product sense and UI/UX design expertise to life. The ideal candidate will have a solid track record in full-stack development, with the ability to design and implement intuitive and engaging user interfaces, as well as architect scalable and efficient backend systems.
What You’ll Do
Full-Stack Development : Design, develop, and maintain both front-end and back-end components of our web applications.
UI/UX Design : Collaborate with design teams to create visually appealing, user-friendly, and accessible UI/UX. You’ll ensure the product provides a seamless experience from end to end.
Backend API Development : Architect, design, and implement RESTful APIs and microservices to support the application.
Collaboration & Mentorship : Work closely with cross-functional teams including product managers, designers, and other engineers. Mentor junior developers and share knowledge of best practices in both UI/UX and back-end development.
Product Sense : Contribute to product strategy by offering insights based on technical feasibility and user experience considerations.
Code Quality & Testing : Write clean, maintainable, and well-documented code. Ensure the reliability and performance of all components with rigorous testing.
Performance Optimization : Continuously monitor and optimize performance, both for the front-end and back-end.
Agile Development : Participate in agile ceremonies, including sprint planning, standups, retrospectives, and code reviews.
What we look for:
5+ years of experience with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
Passion for user experience and design and a deep understanding of front-end architecture.
Comfortable working towards a multi-year vision with incremental deliverables.
Motivated by delivering customer value.
Experience with modern JavaScript frameworks (e.g., React, Angular, or VueJs/Ember).
5+ years of experience with server-side web technologies (eg: Java, Python, Scala, Go).
Good knowledge of SQL.
Experience with cloud technologies, e.g. AWS, Azure, GCP, Docker, or Kubernetes.
Experience developing large-scale distributed systems.
Why Join Us?
Work on AI-powered features that directly impact thousands of data practitioners all over the world.
Collaborate with a world-class team at the intersection of AI, data, and cloud computing.
Build innovative solutions in a fast-moving, high-growth environment.
Ready to shape the future of the Data Intelligence Platform at Databricks? Apply now!

databricks-8540267002.text:
P-1549
At Databricks, we are passionate about enabling data teams to solve the world's toughest problems — from making the next mode of transportation a reality to accelerating the development of medical breakthroughs. We do this by building and running the world's best data and AI infrastructure platform so our customers can use deep data insights to improve their business.
The Mission
Databricks agents are only as good as the context they can retrieve. Whether an agent is answering a question about last quarter's revenue, debugging a failing job, generating SQL against a 10,000-table lakehouse, or summarizing a Wiki page, its quality is bounded by what it can find — and how well it understands what it finds.
We are hiring a Senior Staff Applied AI Engineer to own context retrieval for Databricks agents across SaaS providers . This is a zero-to-one role with two deeply connected charters:
Build the retrieval stack — query understanding, content understanding, ranking, retrieval, and evaluation — across the Enterprise SaaS data stored across multiple systems.
Build the search subagents that sit on top of that stack and reason about what context is needed , how to retrieve it , and whether the right thing actually came back — closing the loop between an agent's intent and the substrate that serves it.
If you have deep Information Retrieval wisdom, have shipped retrieval systems for RAG and agentic workloads, and want to build the substrate — and the agents on top of it — that make every Databricks agent measurably smarter, this role is for you.
What You Will Do
Build the full retrieval stack from scratch. Own the end-to-end system: query understanding, content understanding and indexing, hybrid retrieval, ranking, and evaluation. Make the architectural calls that will define how Databricks agents access context for years to come.
Retrieve across heterogeneous data — structured and unstructured. Index and rank across structured assets (tables, columns, SQL queries, dashboards, code, notebooks, jobs) and unstructured content (docs, wikis, tickets, chat, images, video, audio). Each modality has its own signals — design retrieval that exploits them rather than flattens them.
Connect to the SaaS surface area customers actually use. Build connectors and retrieval adapters for the systems where enterprise knowledge lives. Treat each retrieval source with its own freshness, permissions, and ranking signals.
Optimize for two consumers at once. Retrieval must serve both LLMs (grounded, token-efficient, hallucination-resistant context) and humans (intuitive, explainable discovery). These are different objectives and require different signals — own both.
Crack query understanding for agents. Agent queries don't look like web queries. Build query rewriting, decomposition, intent classification, and entity resolution tuned for multi-turn agentic workflows.
Crack content understanding at scale. Build the pipelines that extract structure, entities, embeddings, summaries, and metadata from every supported asset type — and keep them fresh as customer data evolves.
Build search subagents that reason about retrieval. Design the agentic layer that decides what context is needed , which sources to query , how to decompose and route the search , and — critically — whether the retrieved content is actually sufficient to answer the question . These subagents will plan multi-hop searches, issue follow-up queries when results are weak, ground claims against retrieved evidence, and hand back high-confidence context (or signal failure) to upstream agents. This is where IR meets agentic reasoning.
Build the evaluation flywheel for both retrieval and subagents. Stand up offline evals (nDCG, MRR, Recall@K, Precision@K), LLM-as-judge harnesses, human-in-the-loop labeling, and online experimentation. Extend evaluation beyond ranking metrics to measure subagent decision quality — did it ask the right follow-up? , did it correctly recognize when retrieval failed? , did it ground its answer in the right evidence? . Quality you can't measure is quality you can't ship.
Set technical direction and grow the team. Set the multi-year roadmap, mentor senior engineers, partner with Research, Product, and Platform leaders, and raise the technical bar across the org.
What We're Looking For
10+ years of software engineering experience, with significant time spent building production retrieval, search, or RAG systems at scale.
Deep Information Retrieval (IR) expertise : lexical retrieval (BM25, Lucene/Elasticsearch/OpenSearch), dense retrieval (embeddings, ANN indexes — FAISS, ScaNN, HNSW), hybrid retrieval, and learning-to-rank.
Hands-on experience with modern LLM-era retrieval : RAG architectures, query rewriting, re-ranking with cross-encoders, long-context strategies, and grounding techniques that reduce hallucination.
Experience designing agentic systems on top of retrieval — search planners, multi-hop / iterative retrieval, self-reflection and sufficiency checks, tool-using agents that decide what to fetch and verify what came back.
Strong grasp of relevance evaluation : nDCG, MRR, Precision@K, Recall@K; offline/online experimentation; LLM-as-judge frameworks; building human labeling pipelines.
Experience working across structured and unstructured data — you've indexed and ranked over tables, code, and documents in the same system, and have opinions about how to do it well.
Track record of building 0→1 : you've stood up a retrieval system from an empty repo, made the foundational architectural decisions, and grown it into something that customers depend on.
Demonstrated ability to operate as a technical leader : setting direction across teams, mentoring senior engineers, and influencing roadmap with research, product, and platform partners.
Nice to Have
Experience building retrieval over enterprise SaaS sources (permissions, freshness, multi-tenancy, ACL-aware indexing).
Background in agentic systems, tool use, or multi-turn retrieval for LLM agents.
Contributions to open-source IR/search projects, or publications at SIGIR, KDD, WWW, EMNLP, or similar venues.
Experience training or fine-tuning embedding models, rerankers, or query understanding models.
Why This Role
Foundational impact. Retrieval is the single biggest lever on agent quality. The stack you build will sit underneath every Databricks agent and every customer-built agent on our platform.
Greenfield with scale. You get the rare combination of starting from a clean sheet and having immediate access to massive enterprise scale, real customer data, and a world-class research org.
The right team. You'll work alongside engineers and researchers behind Lakehouse, Apache Spark™, Delta Lake, MLflow, MosaicML, and DBRX.
Location
This role is based in our Mountain View, CA or San Francisco, CA office. Hybrid in-office collaboration expected.

At Databricks, we run the world's largest AI platform. We believe the next breakthroughs will come from models trained on domain-specific enterprise data, not from bigger general-purpose models alone.
That's why we built AI Runtime , a serverless product that makes GPU training of any size feel simple, so companies can train their own models the way frontier labs do. Customers across industries train on it, right next to the enterprise data already in Databricks. Among them are Rivian in automotive, Robinhood in fintech, and Merck, which builds foundation models for drug discovery. Our own AI researchers use it to post-train models with hundreds of billions to nearly a trillion parameters.
It takes a lot of engineering to make that work, and we've written about it on our blog: how we keep GPUs reliable , make training fault-tolerant , and speed up fine-tuning with fused kernels and smart sequence packing. AI agents now launch experiments too, and on our research team they've already increased training jobs 8x .
As a Senior Staff Software Engineer, you'll work on the systems behind all of this, solving the hardest technical problems and shaping where AI Runtime goes next.
The impact you will have:
Drive AI Runtime's architecture and lead Databricks' long-term technical direction in AI training infrastructure.
Define the reliability and observability strategy for a fleet that keeps growing in scale and complexity.
Shape AI Runtime's developer experience for people and agents, so even the largest training jobs feel as simple as a first experiment.
Anticipate industry trends and choose the technical bets that prepare AI Runtime for new GPU generations and workload types.
Take on the hardest multi-node training problems yourself, from orchestration and GPU scheduling to data loading and checkpointing.
Make training faster and cheaper by raising efficiency across model architectures and GPU accelerators.
Work with research, product, and customers to decide what we build next and align teams on hard technical calls.
Champion engineering excellence, raise the bar, and help us hire and grow great engineers.

15+ years in large-scale distributed systems, with significant depth in GPU training, high-performance computing, or ML systems.
Hands-on experience training large models with FSDP, DeepSpeed, or Megatron, and fluency in parallelism strategies.
Expertise in GPU performance, including accelerator architecture, high-speed interconnects, and kernels.
Strong understanding of training resilience patterns, such as checkpointing, failure detection, and automatic recovery.
A background in building and running multi-tenant cloud platforms as products.
A track record of setting technical direction across teams and seeing it through to business impact.
The credibility to bring teams to agreement on difficult trade-offs, and a reputation as a mentor senior engineers seek out.

RDQ427R204
Databricks builds the world's leading data and AI platform, used by tens of thousands of organizations to turn raw data into decisions that matter.
The Lakeflow Engineering team owns the entirety of the ETL product line: Declarative Dataflow Graphs, Materialized Views, Structured Streaming, and Flows. We run what is arguably the world's largest data engineering platform, processing exabytes of data daily across tens of thousands of customers. The problems we solve (fault-tolerant incremental computation, stream-batch unification, declarative pipeline orchestration at massive scale) sit at the frontier of what distributed data systems can do.
We're looking for a Senior Staff Engineer to serve as a technical architect and engineering leader for this platform. You'll own the long-term technical direction for how pipelines are defined, optimized, executed, and operated, shaping the systems that data teams worldwide depend on every day. You will work across one or more of the following areas to design and build the next generation of data infrastructure:
Declarative Dataflow Processing
Resource management
Efficient storage structures
Stream Processing and Complex Event Processing
Autonomic Computing and Self-Managing Systems
The Impact you will have:
Architect and deliver a highly scalable, fault-tolerant platform for declarative pipelines and materialized views serving thousands of production customers.
Turn ambiguous, large-scale technical challenges into clear execution plans that ship incrementally and hold up at exabyte scale.
Bridge the gap between research and production by bringing ideas from the academic literature or internal R&D into systems that solve real customer problems.
Lead deep systems work: performance diagnosis on large production clusters, low-level debugging, and optimization that moves the needle on cost and latency.
Shape product direction alongside engineering and product leadership, owning technical strategy from design through delivery.
Drive complex, multi-team technical initiatives that require sustained coordination and clear technical judgment.
What We’re Looking For:
10+ years of experience building, operating, and evolving large-scale distributed systems in production.
Deep expertise in one or more of: database internals, storage systems, distributed computing, streaming systems, language/API design, or performance engineering.
Track record of executing against a multi-year technical vision through well-sequenced incremental milestones.
Strong algorithmic foundations with the practical judgment to know when they matter and when simpler solutions win.
A bias toward customer impact over technical novelty for its own sake.
Experience building alignment across teams and driving initiatives from conception through customer adoption.
BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science or a related field (or equivalent depth of experience).
